ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Figure (a) shows the circuit connection diagram of an ideal transformer, and Figure (b) shows the relationship between the voltage applied across the primary coil and time. It is known that the voltmeter reading is $20\mathrm{V}$, and the resistances of the two fixed resistors $R$ are both $10\Omega$.

1. What is the turns ratio between the primary and secondary coils?
2. Close the switch $S$, what is the input power of the primary coil?
3. If the ammeter $A_{2}$ is replaced with a unidirectional conducting diode, what will be the voltage reading?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In figure (a), on the left is the primary coil of an ideal transformer; an ammeter A1 is connected in series in the primary-coil circuit, and the primary side is marked with voltage U1; on the right is the secondary coil, an ammeter A2 is connected in series in the secondary-side output circuit, the voltmeter V is connected in parallel at the secondary-side output terminals, and two fixed resistors marked R are connected across the two ends of the secondary side, among which the resistor on the right is controlled by switch S for connection. In figure (b), the voltage u across the two ends of the primary coil changes sinusoidally with time t, the peak value is marked as 200√2 V, and the period is from 0 to 0.02 s. Reasoning: From figure (b), the peak value of the primary-side voltage is read as 200√2 V, so the effective value of the primary side is U1=200 V. The problem gives the voltmeter reading as 20 V, that is, the effective value of the secondary side is U2=20 V. An ideal transformer satisfies U1/U2=N1/N2, therefore N1/N2=200/20=10/1. After closing switch S, the two 10Ω resistors in figure (a) are connected in parallel, and the equivalent resistance is 5Ω; the effective voltage of the secondary side is still 20 V, and the secondary-side output power P=U2^2/R equivalent=20^2/5=80 W. For an ideal transformer, the input power is equal to the output power, so the input power of the primary coil is 80 W. If A2 is replaced with a unidirectionally conducting diode, the secondary-side voltage becomes a half-wave rectified waveform; the primary-secondary turns ratio remains unchanged, the peak value of the secondary-side sinusoidal voltage is 20√2 V, and the effective value of the half-wave rectified voltage is Um/2=(20√2)/2=10√2 V.
